title: VA Budget Shortfall Accountability Act
official_title: To direct the Secretary of Veterans Affairs and the Comptroller General of the United States to report on certain funding shortfalls in the Department of Veterans Affairs.
likelihoodReason: Enacted as Public Law 119-71 on January 20, 2026. Sponsored by Rep. Jack Bergman (R-MI) with 1 cosponsor; per the printed legislative history, the measure passed the House on May 19, 2025 and the Senate on December 18, 2025 before being signed.
summary: Orders GAO to investigate why the VA ran short of money — the fiscal year 2024 shortfall in the Veterans Benefits Administration and the expected fiscal year 2025 shortfall in the Veterans Health Administration — and to repeat the review every year for five years. The VA Secretary must send each report to Congress within 30 days of receiving it.
brief: Requires GAO reviews of the VA's fiscal year 2024 and 2025 funding shortfalls, repeated annually for five years, with every report forwarded to Congress.

items.main: Names the Act the "VA Budget Shortfall Accountability Act".
items.detail: Short-title section — citation name only; no substantive effect.

sections.label: Section 2 — Funding Shortfalls in Certain Administrations of the Department of Veterans Affairs: Reviews; Reports

items.main: Directs the Comptroller General to begin, within 30 days of enactment, a review of the circumstances and causes of the Veterans Benefits Administration's fiscal year 2024 funding shortfall and the expected Veterans Health Administration shortfall in fiscal year 2025.
items.detail: The review must compare monthly obligations and expenditures in the relevant accounts against the VA's spending plan, examine transfers between those accounts, explain any significant diversions from the plan, and analyze the accuracy of the projections behind them. GAO submits a written report of its findings to the VA Secretary within 30 days of completing the review.

items.main: Requires a follow-up GAO review and report in each of the five calendar years after enactment, covering VA funding for the most recent completed fiscal year.
items.detail: Each subsequent review must include the same elements as the first, including remedial actions the Secretary may take to improve the accuracy of the Department's budget-submission supporting information and to prevent future shortfalls. The VA Secretary must forward every GAO report to the House and Senate Veterans' Affairs and Appropriations Committees within 30 days of receiving it.

underreported.summary: Each review must identify remedial actions the Secretary may take to improve the accuracy of supporting information the VA submits for the President's annual budget under section 1105(a) of title 31 and to prevent future funding shortfalls.
underreported.why_unreported: The bill's title and review triggers concern past shortfalls, but this element points GAO at the accuracy of the VA's future budget projections — a forward-looking budget-process element rather than a backward-looking accounting.

gaps: The bill orders reviews of the funding shortfalls but does not itself provide any additional funding to address them.
GAO reports go to the Secretary and four congressional committees, but the bill does not require public release of the findings.
The reviews must list remedial actions the Secretary may take, but nothing in the bill requires the Secretary to adopt any of them.
The bill covers shortfalls in the benefits and health administrations but does not address funding in the Department's other administrations or offices.
